title: Normalize prefetch-induced smoothing in tenant consumption charts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We've observed that the dashboard per-tenant consumption sparkline and per-model breakdowns show overly smooth 'staircase' patterns after a recent prefetch optimization in the ingestion pipeline. Investigation shows the prefetcher batches and emits speculative ledger events ahead-of-time, and our downstream rolling-aggregation window assigns those prefetch events to earlier watermarks. When late/backfilled real events arrive they are merged but the console's projection layer applies a smoothing heuristic (intended for natural jitter) that double-applies on top of prefetch-induced drift, causing under/over-count artifacts in hourly and daily charts.

Goal: Normalize charting and billing telemetry so that prefetch-origin events do not cause permanent smoothing artifacts or misallocated quota display. Ensure billing ledger and customer-visible console charts converge within one hour of actual ingestion, and that backfill runs do not produce visible dips/spikes after reconciliation.

Scope: console projection layer, aggregation watermarking, prefetch tagging in ingestion, reconciliation backfill process, and dashboards' freshness badging. This ticket focuses on detection + mitigation + short-term console-side smoothing removal. Longer-term ingestion rewrite is tracked separately.

Why this matters: Customers are seeing incorrect per-model top-k lists and short-term quota/exhaustion alerts triggered by these artifacts. Finance/CS has flagged two customer support tickets this week where tenants were alerted to quota breaches that reconciled away after backfill. The migration must be visible and reversible via rollback flags.

Links: Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MI/Prefetch+Smoothing+Investigation, Dashboard repro (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/ux/tenant-prefetch-repro, Example customer ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/CS-7841, Early PR with instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4321
tasks:
1) Add explicit 'prefetch' provenance flag to ingest events and propagate through watermarking (Noah)
2) Add non-smoothing path in console projection for prefetch-tagged windows (Ava)
3) Add unit + integration tests to aggregation service to assert idempotent merge semantics for backfilled windows (Ethan)
4) Run targeted synthetic replay for 30 tenants and measure convergence within 1 hour (Maya)
5) Add freshness badge and provenance tooltip to console charts for affected time ranges (Design review: Sophia)
6) Create migration toggle and rollout plan with canary on 5% of traffic (Liam)
7) Postmortem + runbook update after rollout (Ava)
acceptance_criteria:
1) When synthetic prefetch + late events are replayed, console charts converge to expected totals within 60 minutes for 95% of tenants.
2) No new customer-visible spurious quota alerts are generated during the canary rollout.
3) Backfill reconciliation leaves no >1% residual per-model attribution drift across hourly buckets.
4) Freshness badge appears when reconstructed windows exist and links to the provenance timeline.
5) Rollout can be fully reverted via a single toggle with no manual DB migration required.

review_feedback:
PM (Maya Singh): Prioritize customer-visible mitigation first; console badge is minimum viable.
Design (Sophia Martinez): Keep badge text minimal: 'Reconstructed window — values may adjust.' Link to timeline.
Security (Liam O'Connor): No PII in provenance payloads; ensure prefetch flags are size-bounded.
Engineering (Ethan Zhao): Suggest adding a 'reconciled_total' field to projection responses to make diffing easier in the UI.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Reveal-to-customer toggles might increase confusion if too many adjustments appear. Mitigation: Rollout badge as opt-in for canary tenants and include a help article.
Risk: Per-shard watermark changes could shift load and create backpressure. Mitigation: Canary at 5% + autoscaling guardrails + monitor queue depth.
Risk: Backfill reconciliation could create temporary double-charge if ledger dedupe isn't perfect. Mitigation: Add a reconciliation cooldown and ledger-level idempotency keys before enabling billing window reconciliation.
